newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dasa -- no comment on Airbus restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Dasa -- no comment on Airbus restructuring.

text.p: Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa) said on Friday it had no comment to make on a report in news weekly Spiegel that partners in the four-nation Airbus Industrie would agree a restructuring in January.
"Dasa cannot and will not make any comment before the consortium's restructuring talks are completed," a spokesman said in response to an inquiry.

The spokesman added that Dasa favours restructuring the Airbus group into a limited liability company. Chief executive Manfred Bischoff has gone on the record saying such a restructuring could realistically be achieved by late 1998 or early 1999.
Spiegel said on Thursday that a compromise restructuring plan would be signed at a supervisory board meeting on January 3 to turn Airbus into a joint-stock company under French law.
The move aims to better position Airbus to against Boeing and McDonnell-Douglas, which are merging.
Under the plan, France's Aerospatiale, British Aerospace, Dasa and Spain's Casa would bring part of their production facilities as assets into the new company, Spiegel said, quoting unnamed sources.

Dasa would contribute two or three of its five Airbus plants. The partners' plants would be valued by March 1997, by when a new management structure would also be agreed, Spiegel said in extracts of a report to be published on Saturday.

The plan represents a compromise between Anglo-German efforts to bring in as many assets as possible into the new Airbus structure, and fears at Aerospatiale that it would be weakened if it gave up too much of its operating facilities.
Dasa is a unit of auto giant Daimler-Benz AG.
